title: Not-name names.
lede: Sixty famous people who aren't called what you think: musicians, film stars, writers, revolutionaries and a couple of popes. Learn who's really who, a section at a time.

card.title: Not-name names
card.desc: Sixty stage names, pen names and assumed names, and the real names behind them.

groups.label: Music
groups.note: Reggie, Farrokh and a Gordon who looked like a bee.

groups.label: Film & comedy
groups.note: Hollywood loved a rename, and so did the end-of-the-pier circuit.

groups.label: Literature
groups.note: Pen names, for privacy, for a fresh start, or to be taken seriously.

groups.label: Other
groups.note: Revolutionaries, popes, a boxer, a footballer and an escapologist.

items.hook: Borrowed from two bandmates in Bluesology: saxophonist Elton Dean and singer Long John Baldry.
Took “Mercury” from a line in his own song, My Fairy King: “Mother Mercury, look what they've done to me.”
Changed it so as not to be mistaken for Davy Jones of the Monkees. Bowie is after the knife.
Wore a black-and-yellow striped jumper to a gig and looked like a bee. It stuck.
From Bonavox, a hearing-aid shop in Dublin. A friend thought it suited him.
For all the rings he wore, and Starkey shortened to Starr.
The Richard was partly a nod to Little Richard.
From Queen's Radio Ga Ga.
Bruno was a toddler nickname after the wrestler Bruno Sammartino; Mars because, he says, girls told him he was out of this world.
Perry is her mother's maiden name; Katy Hudson was a bit too close to the actress Kate Hudson.
Ike Turner named her Tina, and she kept the surname long after she'd left him.
The first syllable did the job on its own.
A girlfriend said he had eyes like a cat. Later he became Yusuf Islam.
Elvis after Presley; Costello from his family tree.
Iggy from his early band, the Iguanas; Pop from a local character called Jim Popp.
A teacher wrote that William was idle. He took it as a career plan.
A local paper misprinted her surname as Black, and she liked it better.

items.real: Florian Cloud de Bounevialle O'Malley Armstrong
items.hook: Her parents called her Dido from the start. With a name that long, who could blame them?
Known as “Duke” since boyhood, after his dog. The studio chose John Wayne.
A lad from Bristol, who supposedly said: “Everybody wants to be Cary Grant. Even I want to be Cary Grant.”
Monroe was her mother's maiden name.
Picked his name from a poster for The Caine Mutiny while on the phone to his agent in Leicester Square.
His full name is Thomas Cruise Mapother IV. He simply dropped the ends.
Portman was her grandmother's maiden name.
Whoopi as in whoopee cushion, by her own account for reasons of wind.
Women got called up first at open-mic nights, so he chose a name that could be either. Foxx is after Redd Foxx.
Francis Ford Coppola's nephew, who wanted no favours from the name. Cage is after the comic-book hero Luke Cage.
Followed his father: Martin Sheen was born Ramón Estévez. Brother Emilio kept Estevez.
Had to change it: the actors' union already had a Michael Douglas.
Kingsley comes from his grandfather's nickname, “King Clove”, from his days trading spices.
Her father anglicised the family name when she was a child.
Dropped Jefferson partly because “Stan Jefferson” had thirteen letters, which he thought unlucky.
Named himself after his home town.
Orwell is a river in Suffolk.
“Mark twain” is a riverboat call: two fathoms of water, safe to pass.
Charles Lutwidge, put into Latin as Carolus Ludovicus, reversed and turned back into English.
Wrote as a man to be taken seriously, and to keep her private life private.
Seuss was his middle name and his mother's maiden name. The doctorate was entirely self-awarded.
A serving MI6 officer, who couldn't publish under his own name.
Stalin means man of steel. He chose it himself, naturally.
Borrowed the name from one of his jailers in Odessa.
Took her name from Saint Thérèse of Lisieux.
Chose Francis after Saint Francis of Assisi, the first pope ever to use it.
The first American pope, elected in 2025.
Changed it in 1964 on joining the Nation of Islam, calling Cassius Clay his slave name.
Where “Pelé” came from is a mystery, even to Pelé, who said he didn't like it at first.
Nicknamed after a Vietnamese soldier and friend of his father's, also known as Tiger.
Houdini after the French magician Robert-Houdin; Harry from his childhood nickname, Ehrie.
Named for her very thin legs.
